name: Ambient bass with a solid floor: one mono voice with light unison, a single slow retriggered master LFO (about 4 bars) on many timbre targets (wavetable position, both filter cutoffs, drive, formant, FX filter) so everything moves together, an FM macro for grit, and a clean sine sub sent direct-out past the filter while the upper layers are high-passed
goal: Make an ambient bass that guides the track with subtle, unified movement but keeps a solid low end: one mono voice, one slow master LFO driving many timbre parameters at once so the motion feels glued, an FM/osc-mix macro for extra character, and a plain sine sub routed around the filter and effects while the moving layers are high-passed above it. Everything below about 100-120 Hz stays mono.

source.title: Get BETTER ambient bass EVERY time

prerequisites: Wavetable or hybrid synth with mono mode, unison, a mod matrix with many LFO destinations, two filters, distortion/FX and a sub or extra oscillator that can bypass the filter (direct out)
EQ with high-pass and a bass-mono/stereo-width utility

inputs.name: bass_notes
inputs.description: Long, mostly static root notes under the track

outputs.name: ambient_bass_patch
outputs.description: Mono bass with unified slow motion and a clean sine floor

outputs.name: bass_audio
outputs.description: Bass render that moves subtly but sits solidly

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Mono below about 100-120 Hz: either one synth voice or a bass-mono utility at 100-120 Hz.
Movement stays subtle: 'a little bit of motion goes a long way'. The master LFO moves timbre only, never pitch.
Steady pitch (Matt's taste): no random pitch or detune wobble; keep unison detune small and static. Unison here is slight and its detune is not modulated.
Rebuild with original/free wavetables; no presets or patch packs.
Drums early (Matt's taste): if the track has drums, the kick/drum loop enters by about count 8 (roughly 10-12 s), with only pad before that.

Polyrhythm Studio / Web Audio mapping: OscillatorNode + GainNode per layer, BiquadFilterNode (lowpass/highpass/allpass) for filters, DelayNode/ConvolverNode for space, AudioParam automation or slow custom LFOs for movement.
Auto-generated YouTube Show transcript; values are as spoken and approximate where the speaker says 'about' or 'around'.

steps.action: Set the bass to a single voice (mono) and add light unison (the source uses 5 voices on two oscillators) for subtle motion that shows on an oscilloscope without smearing the low end.
steps.expect: A mono bass with gentle internal movement

steps.action: Make one master LFO: retriggered on each note, slow (about 4 bars per cycle), and route it to many destinations at small amounts: wavetable position on both oscillators, filter 1 and filter 2 cutoff, distortion amount, spectral morph/harmonic stretch, a negative formant scale, and the FX distortion's filter and drive.
steps.expect: All timbre parameters drift together, so the sound stays unified and gets slightly grittier as the cycle peaks

steps.action: Add an FM macro: osc 2 frequency-modulates osc 1 (and vice versa), and the same macro brings in an offset distortion that only starts once FM is applied. Try it an octave up if it is muddy.
Add an osc-mix macro that fades a third oscillator in from zero.
For a solid floor, set a sub/extra oscillator to a plain sine with no LFO modulation and route it direct out (past the filter and effects).
steps.expect: A stable sine sub that does not phase or move

steps.action: Put a high-pass EQ on the moving layers (or the full patch before the sub joins) so they are cut at the low end and leave room for the sine; balance the sub level by ear.
steps.expect: Oscilloscope shows a clean sine at the bottom with the movement above it

steps.action: Apply bass mono below about 100-120 Hz on the channel (or rely on the single voice), and A/B in the track: the bass should stand out a little and guide the track without dominating.
steps.expect: Long static notes that still feel like they are going somewhere

verification: The patch is mono (one voice) or mono below 100-120 Hz.
One LFO drives at least 5 timbre destinations, and none of them is pitch.
The sine sub is unmodulated and bypasses the filter; the moving layers are high-passed above it.
Held notes change timbre slowly over about 4 bars without audible pitch wobble.
